source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: Rice caseworm (Nymphula depunctalis) moths are white with small black or grayish-brown spots and a fringed wing margin; eggs are laid in clusters underneath rice leaves. The larva builds a floating tube-like case out of cut leaf pieces, uses it as a shield, and feeds by cutting/scraping leaf tissue from inside the flooded field; the pupa forms with white waxy threads and rests at the water surface. Damage is worst when standing water is deep during early tillering through booting, since the floating larva depends on standing water to move between leaves and feed; larvae also travel between hills by drifting on the water surface at night. Draining excess standing water and maintaining only shallow water is one of the cultural controls the deck associates specifically with this pest.
